documents.t: Worked examples — executed notebooks rendered as pages (refreshed weekly against the live APIs): Quickstart

sportsdataverse.basketball.bleague — 14 endpoints. Note: Unofficial and unsupported: the game contexts are JSON objects in B.LEAGUE's own public S3 bucket (b-league.s3.amazonaws.com, the store its game pages read), and schedule / standings / game_detail are pages of www.bleague.jp parsed here. Neither host publishes terms for this use (the site's /terms/ answers 404; robots.txt sets a Crawl-delay only for msnbot and bingbot), and bleague_runtime spaces requests at least 1 s apart. SportsDataverse has not ruled on the site's terms, so payloads are not redistributed as release assets. Note: Seasons: the site's Year is the season START year; every wrapper takes season, the END year (2026 = 2025-26), and bleague_runtime sends season - 1. Game wrappers take the global schedule_key (one integer sequence across B1, B2, B3 and every season: 1 = the 2016-17 opener, 5856 in 2020-21, 500017 in 2022-23, 504734 / 505508 B1 / B2 and 10693 B3 in 2025-26); list a day's keys with bleague_schedule. The runtime reads the feed at run time: v2 (B1/B2 from 2020-21), then v1 (B3 and B1/B2 2018-2020), then the game page's embedded copy (the only source of 2016-17 and 2017-18). Note: Coverage: game wrappers serve FINISHED games only (an unfinished game raises AssetFetchError; 2019-20 game 4153 is an unfinished feed). The two feeds differ: v2 ids are strings, v1 ids integers (both become text here); v1 adds leaders and the score track; the team-rebound codes 18 / 19 are swapped between them and a v1 substitution is one row where v2 has two (see bleague_pbp). Shot x / y exist from 2022-23 on v2 only, side from 2025-26; before that bleague_shots is empty. Player and team names are Japanese (English names only on the box score and header); the code tables are in bleague_codes.
